newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa firmer but off highs after grind data.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa firmer but off highs after grind data.

text.p: CSCE cocoa was firmer at midsession but down from early highs after a strong showing on the U.S. first quarter grind failed to propel the market through key resistance levels, traders said.

U.S. cocoa grindings -- which reflect the amount of cocoa processed by manufacturers -- rose a hefty 20.74 percent on the year, more than double what most market participants had anticipated. But after an initial rally to the day's highs, the buying momentum all but fizzled, dealers said.
"Speculative buying took the market up, but some trade selling came in," a trader said. "It's drifting aimlessly at this point."
At 1204 EDT, benchmark July futures were $13 higher at $1,464 a tonne, well below the $1,473 peak scaled early. Spot May was $17 higher, at $1,435.
While the sharp year-on-year increase in grindings was widely seen as bullish, traders said the news would be overshadowed in the long run by crop production figures from top-grower Ivory Coast.
Arrivals at Ivorian ports totalled some 970-980,000 tonnes as of April 14, exporters and analysts said, only slightly below last season's record of just over a million tonnes.
((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
